text: . Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight, including hundreds targeting Moscow. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin called it the largest-ever drone attack on the capital, reporting damage to an oil refinery and a residential building. Mr Sobyanin said, two people were killed and 20 injured in the attcak across wider Moscow region. Russia’s Ministry of Defence said, its forces shot down 1,100 Ukrainian drones across the country.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, Kyiv had used a range of missiles and drones in the attack, including Ukraine’s domestically made Flamingo and Pelican missiles to hit oil and logistics facilities.Both Russia and Ukraine have continued to hit energy infrastructure targets in the past week, despite US President Donald Trump claiming on social media that the two sides had agreed not to do so.

. Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh and Japan Air Self-Defense Force Chief of Staff General Takehiro Morita flew together in India’s indigenous Light Combat Aircraft Tejas during a formation sortie in Jodhpur today. The flight by the air chiefs of both nations comes as the Indian Air Force and Japan Air Self-Defense Force are conducting the joint air exercise ‘Veer Guardian 2026’ in Jodhpur.This is the first time that Japanese fighter aircraft are operating from Indian soil as part of a bilateral exercise, further deepening the defence partnership between both the countries.Talking to media in Jodhpur after the sortie, Air Chief Marshall Singh said, first-ever operation of Japanese fighter jet on Indian soil marks major milestone in bilateral defence ties.The Japanese Air Chief appreciated the warm hospitality extended by the Indian side and described the Tejas as a symbol of India’s technological innovation and the country’s Make in India initiativeThe 14-day exercise, which will conclude on Tuesday, focuses on advanced operational missions and extensive professional interactions between the two air forces. The exercise involves a diverse mix of Indian Air Force frontline combat aircraft, including the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale while Japan is participating with F-2A fighter aircraft.

. The Indian tennis team was knocked out of the 2026 Davis Cup after suffering a 3-1 defeat to the Republic of Korea in their second-round qualifier in Seoul today. Sumit Nagal’s singles loss handed the hosts an unassailable lead and secured their place in the Final 8.India, who began the day trailing 2-0 after losing both opening singles matches yesterday, briefly revived their hopes when N. Sriram Balaji and Dhakshineswar Suresh won the doubles match to reduce the deficit. However, world No. 157 Kwon Soon-woo defeated India’s top-ranked singles player Nagal 6-1, 6-2 to seal the tie for South Korea, who will compete in the Final 8 in Bologna, Italy, in November.The defeat means India will have to compete in the first round of the 2027 Davis Cup Qualifiers. World No. 49 doubles pair Balaji and Suresh had kept India in contention with a 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 victory over South Korea’s Nam Ji-sung and Park Ui-sung.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The global ratings agency Moody’s today raised India’s real GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent, ​from its earlier projection of 6 per cent for the current financial year. The agency said that the upward revision reflects the resilience of the Indian economy amid the global shock caused by the conflict in West Asia.The agency expects India to continue growing faster than all other G20 economies. Moody’s said India’s real GDP growth rose to 8.2 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, compared with 7.3 per cent in 2025. The growth was supported by stronger private consumption, robust investment, continued government spending on infrastructure, a revival in private investment and sustained strength in the services sector. However, Moody’s has warned of risks to the outlook.El Niño-related disruptions could push up food prices and affect private consumption. Higher energy and fertiliser import costs, weaker external demand and lower remittances from West Asia could also widen the current account deficit and slow economic growth.

. India’s textile exports increased to over 29,700 crore rupees in August this year as compared to over 25,600 crore rupees during same month of the last year. The Ministry of Textiles said that the exports increased by 16.1 per cent as compared to August 2025. It added that during April-August 2026, cumulative textile exports reached over 1,40,000 crore rupees, registering growth of 10.3 per cent over the corresponding period of the previous year.The Ministry said that the sustained growth across major segments reflects the increasing competitiveness and diversification of India’s textile export basket. It added that the growth is supported by improved market access, policy interventions and continued efforts towards value addition and market diversification.

. US President Donald Trump will meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in New York tomorrow to push efforts to secure de-escalation between Russia and Ukraine, with the two leaders expected to discuss steps towards reducing hostilities and reviving negotiations. The meeting is being organised on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. Ukrainian chief negotiator Rustem Umerov, who also heads Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service, has been working with White House envoys to arrange the talks.The planned meeting follows a phone conversation between Trump and Zelenskyy, during which the two leaders agreed to meet in New York. Zelenskyy described the conversation as important and said it had generated diplomatic momentum. Trump repeatedly urged Zelenskyy during the call to halt Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, with the attacks being linked to disruptions in fuel supplies and higher diesel prices. A source familiar with the conversation told Axios that “the word diesel came up many times during the call.”The issue of energy infrastructure has emerged as an important element of US efforts to reduce tensions between Moscow and Kyiv. Zelenskyy has previously indicated that Ukraine could halt strikes on Russian energy facilities if Russia provides firm guarantees against attacks on Ukrainian critical infrastructure.

. In the Asian Games, India secured a double podium finish in the men’s 10-metre air rifle event in Nagoya, Japan. Himanshu Dhillon won the silver medal with a score of 252.4, while Rudrankksh Patil clinched the bronze with 230.9. Earlier, India had also won the silver medal in the men’s 10-metre air rifle team event.The Indian trio of Himanshu Dhillon, Parth Mane and Rudrankksh Patil finished second with a total score of 1890.1, behind China’s score of 1899.0. In Mixed Martial Arts, Suchika Tariyal bagged the bronze medal after losing 0-2 to Singapore’s Hui Hoon Toe in the women’s 60-kilogram traditional semi-final.Earlier, Elavenil Valarivan, Vidarsa Vinod and Sonam Maskar won silver in the women’s 10-metre air rifle team event, while Elavenil also claimed silver in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Individual event, finishing just behind Japan’s Hinata Taichi.

. The United States has issued a security alert for its mission in Saudi Arabia, requiring US government employees working in the country to obtain special authorisation for all official and personal travel to the cities of Taif and Yanbu. The US Mission in Saudi Arabia said the restrictions were imposed “due to the ongoing security situation” and urged American citizens in the kingdom to remain vigilant and follow recommended security measures. The mission said regular and emergency consular services remained available for US citizens.The alert comes after Yemen’s Houthi group launched attacks towards Saudi Arabia, including a ballistic missile directed at Riyadh. Saudi-led coalition forces said the missile was intercepted. Houthi also attempted attacks targeting civilian populations and infrastructure in Bish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu. The latest escalation has prompted heightened security measures across the kingdom. Saudi authorities issued an emergency warning over a “hostile aerial threat”. An explosion and a large plume of smoke were reported near Riyadh’s airport. Saudi authorities reported no casualties or damage from the Riyadh incident.The US Mission has advised Americans in Saudi Arabia to enrol in the Department of State’s Smart Traveller Enrollment Program (STEP), monitor local media and official announcements, keep their phones charged and follow instructions from Saudi authorities. It also advised US citizens to stay away from windows and glass doors in the event of an aerial attack, avoid demonstrations and large gatherings, exercise caution at locations publicly associated with the United States and maintain a low profile. The State Department currently maintains a Level 3 “Reconsider Travel” advisory for Saudi Arabia, citing risks including Iranian drone and missile attacks, armed conflict and terrorism.US government employees are already subject to additional restrictions in areas including the Yemen border region, Jizan, Asir, Najran and Qatif. Meanwhile, Qatar has strongly condemned the Houthi attacks, including the ballistic missile targeting Riyadh and attempted strikes on civilian populations and infrastructure in Bish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu. Qatar’s Foreign Ministry described the attacks as a violation of Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and international law and expressed solidarity with the kingdom. The United States has separately warned Americans travelling to or through West Asia to remain vigilant amid heightened regional tensions, citing the possibility of flight cancellations, airspace closures and other disruptions.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. In a historic first, Angh, directed by Naga filmmaker Theja Rio, has won the Platform Prize 2026 at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF). Angh was one of 12 films selected for this year’s platform programme, the TIFF’s only competitive section. Beginning with the 2026 prize, winning the TIFF Platform Prize gives a non-English-language film a direct pathway to eligibility for consideration for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film. Announcing the award, Jury President Pablo Trapero praised Angh for its refreshing perspective, strength of filmmaking and deeply resonant portrait of a world.The jury also commended Theja Rio for his vision, audacity and courage. In his acceptance speech, Theja Rio thanked the TIFF jury and said the recognition was truly special, as it highlights a film from an Indigenous region and in a tribal language. He said it meant a great deal to the team to represent their people and receive the award. He also thanked his family and friends for their unwavering support. Rio said he came from a small part of Northeast India, where, he noted, dreams do not often come true for his people. He dedicated the award to the people back home, saying that this is just the beginning. The Platform programme champions films with bold directorial vision and distinctive storytelling. The Platform Prize carries a cash award of 20,000 Canadian dollars and a trophy.The Platform jury this year comprised Pablo Trapero, Amma Asante, Sylvia Chang, Luc Déry and Albert Lee. Nagaland Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio has congratulated Director Theja Rio and the team of ‘ANGH’ on winning the prestigious Platform Prize at the Toronto International Film Festival, TIFF. In a social media post, the Chief Minister said the historic win marks a proud moment for Nagaland and India, and carries a Naga debut onto the Oscar journey. He added that it is also a proud moment for the region and its storytellers on the global stage as ‘ANGH’ brings Naga cinema and its talent into the spotlight. Mr Rio extended his best wishes to the entire team for their journey ahead.

. US President Donald Trump has said that he is in deciding mode over the Iran war, warning that big things are going to happen. His remarks came after Tehran said it has shared its conditions with Washington, through mediators, for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Trump’s comments come ahead of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s expected visit to New York to attend the United Nations General Assembly. A senior delegation is likely to accompany him.Trump told a TV channel that very big things are going to be happening in the not-so-distant future if the Iranian regime does not behave. He reportedly discussed three possible options for the war – “wiping Iran out”, “letting them rot economically”, or “making a deal”. Iran has communicated seven conditions to the United States through Qatar to resume negotiations aimed at bringing the ongoing war to an end.Regarding other conflicts in the region, Trump said Washington remains in contact with Yemen’s Houthi rebels following their recent ballistic missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia. He added that the group has agreed not to attack American personnel.

. India’s Women’s Badminton team made a winning start to its Asian Games campaign, with a 3-NIL win over Kazakhstan in the pre-quarterfinal in Aichi, Japan, today. P.V. Sindhu set the tone for India with a dominant 21-7, 21-9 win over Kamila Smagulova in the opening singles rubber. Unnati Hooda then extended India’s advantage with an equally convincing 21-7, 21-10 victory over Alissa Kuleshova. Tanvi Sharma completed the clean sweep with an emphatic 21-5, 21-10 victory over Diana Namenova. India will next face second seeds and hosts Japan in the quarter finals. Japan received a bye in their first-round.

. The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) organised an interactive Talkathon on the theme ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ today on the call of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a drug-free India. The CBSE said, that the 45-minute programme brought together experts, educators and students to discuss issues related to substance abuse, prevention and the importance of making healthy and responsible choices. The initiative aimed to directly engage students through social media platforms. CBSE invited questions from students and they raised questions concerning mental health, peer pressure and steps for de-addiction.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was one per cent up at 1,52,362 rupees per 10 grams. Silver rose 1.1 per cent to 2,31,337 rupees per kilogram.

. In the Asian Games 2026, India’s campaign continues strongly on Day 2 in Japan today. Indian shooters secured 2 Silver medals in Nagoya today. India’s Elavenil Valarivan clinched a silver medal in the women’s 10 metre air rifle event at the Games. The 2025 World Championship bronze medallist Elavenil shot 252.4 points in the final to finish behind Japan’s Hinata Taichi, who won gold with a record 253 points.Earlier, India has secured the silver medal in the women’s 10 metre air rifle team event, with Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod combining to deliver the country’s first medal of the Games. Sonam top-scored for India with 634.1, finishing fourth in the individual qualification, while Olympian Elavenil finished seventh with 633.5 points. China took the gold medal with a total score of 1904.2, while India held on to second spot by scoring 1897.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated the team on winning the Medal. In a social media post, she said that this commendable achievement has opened India’s medal account at the Games and brings immense pride to the nation.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has paid tribute to Lakshmanrao Inamdar on his birth anniversary today. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that Lakshmanrao Inamdar empowered society through his national service, organisation building, and cooperation. The Home Minister added that Lakshmanrao Inamdar gave a new direction and momentum to the cooperative movement in Gujarat and shaped numerous activists like a guardian. He said that the life of Lakshmanrao Inamdar remains an inspiration for all.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. The Consulate General of India in Vancouver has expressed condolences on the tragic demise of Manoj Sivakumar and Srisaran Thirugnanasambantham, two Indian students from Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, who lost their lives in a tragic air accident in Canada during their flight training. In a social media post, the consulate stated that they are with the bereaved families and loved ones during this difficult time. The Consulate stands ready to extend all possible consular assistance to the families in connection with the repatriation of the mortal remains to India.

. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has paid respects to Amrita Devi Bishnoi and all the martyrs who laid down their lives for the protection of Khejri trees in Khejadli village of Rajasthan during the 18th century. On Khejadli Sacrifice Day today, Mr Birla said that the memory of those environment-loving sacrificers remains an integral part of Rajasthan’s folk consciousness to this day.In a social media post, he said that the story of Khejadli tells that the concept of environmental conservation is neither new nor modern in India. He added that Rajasthan is not only renowned for its tales of valour, sacrifice, and heroism, but also for a profound tradition of deep faith in nature. The Lok Sabha Speaker further said that the story of Khejadli reminds the citizens of their responsibility towards the environment around them.

. India has been ranked first in business climate among forty plus global markets in the latest Business Climate Survey 2026 by the Swedish Chamber of Commerce in India. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal shared this information in a social media post. He said India’s business climate is setting the gold standard for stability, growth and ease of doing business amid global turbulence.The Global Business Climate Survey 2026 edition presents insights from 41 markets, offering a broad view of Swedish companies’ perspectives on doing business abroad. The survey aims to provide a framework for comparing economic performance, outlook, and operating conditions over time in key Swedish export markets. It highlights the challenges companies face and identifies opportunities for Swedish companies considering entry into new markets or expansion in existing ones.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Parth Rakesh Mane and Himanshu Dhillon on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, she said that their precision and outstanding performance have brought great pride to the nation. President Murmu extended best wishes to them for many more laurels ahead.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. Iran has ruled out reopening the Strait of Hormuz or returning to the previous framework of negotiations with the United States until Washington meets Tehran’s conditions, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said, as tensions between the two countries continue to escalate.Mr Ghalibaf said Iran has conveyed its demands to the United States through intermediaries and would not reconsider its position until Tehran’s conditions were fulfilled. The Strait of Hormuz has emerged as a major flashpoint in the escalating US-Iran confrontation. The strategic waterway is a crucial route for global energy shipments, and restrictions on maritime traffic have raised concerns over further disruption to international trade and oil supplies.Ghalibaf’s remarks came after Iran’s central military command warned that any renewed US military action against Tehran would trigger attacks against American bases and interests across the region.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. India and Nepal discussed measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry in a statement said that during the two day meeting of Inter-Governmental Sub-Committee (IGSC) on Trade, Transit and Cooperation to Control Unauthorised Trade which concluded yesterday both sides reviewed a wide range of issues. It was related to market access, Customs and trade facilitation, standards, food safety, border infrastructure, rail and road connectivity and other trade-related matters.The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Department of Commerce, Ujjwal Kumar Ghosh, while the Nepali delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Buddha Bahadur Gurung. The meeting focused on facilitating legitimate trade while strengthening mechanisms to ensure compliance with applicable rules and prevent misuse of preferential trade arrangements. Both sides also reviewed rail and road connectivity, movement of freight, Integrated Check Posts and land-port infrastructure.The discussions focused on improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure and addressing operational bottlenecks affecting bilateral and transit trade. The Ministry said that India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and economic ties and the discussions at the IGSC are expected to further strengthen bilateral trade, transit connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar will lead the Indian delegation for the High Level Week at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, USA. The External Affairs Minister is scheduled to address the High-Level Session of the 81st UNGA on the 26th of this month. During the visit, Dr Jaishankar will also attend various multilateral and bilateral meetings.Dr Jaishankar’s visit to New York comes as world leaders prepare to gather at the UN headquarters for the annual high-level General Debate, scheduled from September 22 to 28. The 81st session of the UN General Assembly is being held under the theme “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.”The General Assembly will bring together presidents, prime ministers and senior representatives from all 193 UN member states, who will outline their priorities and positions on major international issues. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called on world leaders to strengthen international cooperation as they gather in New York for the General Assembly.In a video message, Guterres said, “Come together for peace, dignity, justice, and humanity. Only with international cooperation we can build a better world. Guterres is attending his final UN General Assembly as Secretary-General, with his tenure set to conclude later this year. According to the United Nations, the 81st session will focus on revitalising global cooperation, advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and promoting collective action for peace, dignity and equality.The UN General Assembly’s high-level week will also feature discussions on global conflicts, development, climate change, humanitarian challenges and other pressing international issues. The General Debate is expected to provide a major platform for leaders to present their foreign policy priorities and engage on key global developments.

. In Sudan, 10 artisanal miners have been killed and 21 others injured after five mining shafts collapsed in the Oni area of Red Sea State in the eastern part of the country. The Sudanese Mineral Resources Company has confirmed the mine collapse. The accident occurred on Saturday when adjacent underground shafts collapsed one after another, burying miners under rock and soil. Difficult access to parts of the mining site has hampered rescue operations and made it difficult to determine the exact number of missing miners.

. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has cautioned that the semiconductor industry should be prepared for cyberattacks and any kind of disruption by countries that do not want India to move up the semiconductor value chain.Talking to a media house in New Delhi, Mr Vaishnaw said India has to continuously be watchful of the potential geopolitical risks that will arise because it is now emerging as a country that can design and manufacture chips. He added that this will be seen as a threat by many other established players. Mr Vaishnaw said it is an industry which requires lots of effort on every front. He added that the industry, the government, and the state governments have to work in tandem.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya has congratulated Suchika Tariyal for winning the bronze medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) Women’s Traditional-60 kg category at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, Mr Mandaviya said that this is a historic moment as it is India’s first-ever MMA medal at the Asian Games. Dr Mandaviya has also congratulated Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Parth Rakesh Mane and Himanshu Dhillon on securing the Silver Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games 2026.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya congratulated Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa K Vinod on winning a silver medal in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, Dr Mandaviya wished the champions and the entire Indian contingent many more moments of glory.

. Union Minister of New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi has congratulated Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) on its 15th Foundation Day today. In a social media post, Mr Joshi said that SECI has played an important role in advancing India’s renewable energy journey and strengthening the country’s clean energy ecosystem over the past 15 years.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through the premier state-of-the-art convention and exhibition complexes like Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi.Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi are India’s world class Exhibition cum Convention complexes designed to position India as a global leader in MICE, which stands for Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Yashobhoomi at Dwarka in New Delhi in September 2023. The Convention Center comprises 15 convention rooms including the Main auditorium, the Grand ballroom and 13 meeting rooms with a total capacity of holding 11,000 delegates. Bharat Mandapam was dedicated to the nation by the Prime Minister in July 2023.Bharat Mandapam has hosted key global gatherings like the G20 Leaders’ Summit and the recently held BRICS Summit. Its majestic multi-purpose hall and plenary hall have a combined capacity of seven thousand people, which is larger than the seating capacity of the famous Sydney Opera House in Australia.Inaugurating Bharat Mandapam, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the Exhibition cum Convention Centre will give a boost to Conference Tourism in the country. He said it will also facilitate national and international exhibitors.Talking to Akashvani News, Hrithik, a student who attended and volunteered at many events in Bharat Mandapam said the venue is truly world-class and has changed the event scene in India.Today, both Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi have become the biggest hubs of conference tourism in the country. With Suparna Saikia, Anupam Mishra, Akashvani News, Delhi.

. Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel today said that India’s journey in Pharmacovigilance has been a remarkable example of self-reliance over the years. She said this while releasing the 7th Edition of the National Formulary of India in New Delhi. The Minister said that currently more than one thousand one hundred Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring Centres are operational in the country and the Government aims to increase this number up to the primary health facility level.She informed that the country now provides pharmacovigilance data to the WHO patient safety database. The Minister further highlighted that India has risen from the 123rd rank in 2014 to 8th rank in providing this data to WHO. She also said that 25 countries in the world recognise and accept the Indian pharmacopoeia. On the occasion, the Minister appealed the citizens to avoid any form of self-medication, follow professional prescriptions, and never ignore a sudden or unexpected side effect of any medicinal drug.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. In Nepal, Search operations continued today for around 6,000 people still unaccounted for after nearly four weeks of devastating flash floods that killed more than 1,400 people.Search operations have continued along river stretches, debris fields and damaged hydropower projects in Rasuwa and neighbouring districts. Earlier this month, a Nepal Army field commander said clearing debris from some of the affected tunnels could take three to four months because of the volume and condition of the material.The disaster has also left large parts of the affected region struggling with damaged roads and bridges. The government has begun repairing suspension bridges along the Trishuli corridor after the August 26 floods destroyed or damaged crossings connecting communities in Nuwakot and Dhading.The flash floods, which originated near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 2026, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal. Forty-three people were killed on the Chinese side of the border. According to Chinese media, more than 500 people still remain missing in China.

. In Hockey, the Indian Men’s team opened their Asian Games campaign with a 13-1 win over Indonesia today, in their Pool A game in Kakamigahara, Japan. Dilpreet Singh’s four-goal haul led the team towards victory. While  Abhishek, Rajinder Singh, Mandeep Singh, captain Harmanpreet Singh and Jugraj Singh added one apiece. Indonesia’s lone goal came from Aulia Al Ardh in the 33rd minute. The Indian team next faces Sri Lanka on Tuesday.Earlier, Indian Women’s team began their campaign with a dominant 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their Pool B opener at Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium. Deepika Sehrawat was the star of the match scoring eight goals. Ishika Chaudhary scored three, while Lalthantluangi and Neha bagged two each. Indian Women’s team will next take on Indonesia tomorrow.The opening result gave India an early platform in the tournament, with their forwards and penalty-corner attack both making an immediate impact.

The Indian men’s chess team secured an emphatic 3-1 victory over Holland, while the Indian women’s team suffered a shocking defeat to Poland in the fifth round of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The Indian men extended their perfect run to five consecutive match wins, placing them at the top of the leaderboards alongside Uzbekistan and Germany.R Praggnanandhaa bounced back from a string of draws to score a brilliant victory over an in-form Anish Giri. Arjun Erigaisi fought hard to secure a draw against Jorden Van Foreest. Nihal Sarin comfortably held a draw against veteran Loek Van Wely. D Gukesh continued his sublime form by defeating Erwin l’Ami, picking up his fourth individual win in five games.Indian women’s team faced their first major speed bump of the tournament. A critical loss by R Vaishali proved costly, as the rest of the squad couldn’t make up the deficit, resulting in a narrow 1.5-2.5 defeat. This loss dropped the women’s team to eighth place, though six rounds still remain to mount a comeback.

In the Chess Olympiad, the Indian men’s team defeated Spain 3-1, with world champion D Gukesh leading the way with a clean victory over former world championship challenger Alexei Shirov in Samarkand yesterday. Meanwhile, R Praggnanandhaa was held to a draw by David Anton Guijarro, while Nihal Sarin also settled for a draw against Jaime Santos Latasa. In the women’s section, India recorded a 3-1 victory over Mongolia. B Savitha Shri continued her impressive run with her fourth consecutive win, defeating seasoned player Munguntuul Batkhuyag.

The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Delhi Zonal Office, has provisionally attached equity shares of a company having a current market value of more than Rs 42 Crore, in connection with an alleged large-scale financial fraud involving a collective investment scheme.ED initiated the investigation based on an FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation. Subsequently, CBI filed a charge-sheet and a supplementary charge-sheet against 33 accused persons for their role in running the illegal investment scheme.According to the charge-sheets, the accused entities and persons were fraudulently mobilising over Rs 48,000 crore from lakhs of investors across India under the pretext of sale and development of agricultural land. Investors were induced to invest and made to sign misleading documents, such as agreements, powers of attorney, and other instruments. In most cases, land was never delivered, and approximately Rs 48,000 crore remains unpaid to investors.ED has attached over 29.46 lakh equity shares of the company, purchased for more than Rs 30 Crore. The agency alleged that the funds used for the purchases were diverted from money mobilised from gullible investors. Further investigation is in progress.

. President Droupadi Murmu will be on a three-day visit to Gujarat beginning today. She will preside over the presentation ceremony of the 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar, Kevadia, tomorrow. Akashvani correspondent reports that the National Film Awards, recognising achievements in Indian cinema for the year 2024, will be presented by the President tomorrow. Instituted in 1954, the National Film Awards are among the country’s highest honours for excellence in cinema. Presented annually by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the awards recognise creative and technical achievements across feature films, non-feature films and writing on cinema.The winners of the 72nd edition were announced on July 18, 2026, by the chairpersons of the three juries. The awards are divided into three main sections – Feature Films, Non-Feature Films and Best Writing on Cinema – along with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the highest honour in Indian cinema. The Feature Film section includes awards for Best Feature Film, Best Direction, acting, cinematography, music direction and costume design, among others.The Non-Feature Film section covers documentaries, short films, animation, arts and culture films, narration or voice-over and script. The Best Writing on Cinema section recognises the best book on cinema and the best film critic. The Dadasaheb Phalke Award follows a separate process, with a specially constituted committee of eminent film personalities recommending the recipient.

United Nations (UN) Secretary-General Antonio Guterres today urged world leaders to come together for peace, dignity, justice and humanity as they prepare to attend the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York for his final session as Secretary-General.In a video message on social media post Mr. Guterres said international cooperation, dialogue and collective action were essential to addressing global challenges.Mr Guterres said, this is his last UNGA as Secretary-General and said international dialogue, cooperation and collective action is now needed more than ever.The 81st UNGA session from 22 to 28 of this month, brings together leaders from all 193 member states to discuss global challenges and advance cooperation, Sustainable Development Goals and collective action for peace and equality.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.
